fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Jesus says, "…everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man will be fulfilled." (Luke 18:31) The prophets were the ones holding the pen. Jesus says what they wrote will be fulfilled.

Not quite, friend. Jesus says the Son of Man "…will be delivered over to the Gentiles and will be mocked and insulted and spit upon." (Luke 18:32) There's no guest treatment in that verse. It's a heavy one, and the mocking is what He says.

Hearing isn't what the text points to, friend. Jesus "…took the Twelve aside…" and spoke to them (Luke 18:31). The text says, "The meaning was hidden from them, and they did not comprehend what He was saying." (Luke 18:34) So the reason it gives is the hidden meaning.
No governor in that verse, friend. The people tell him, "Jesus of Nazareth is passing by…" (Luke 18:37) That's the answer they give. The man asked what was happening, and that's what he hears.

A wedding party isn't what they say, baker. They tell him, "Jesus of Nazareth is passing by…" (Luke 18:37) He heard the crowd going by and asked what was happening (Luke 18:36). That's the answer he gets.
Right, baker. He calls out, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" (Luke 18:38) He sits there begging, yet the thing he asks Jesus for is mercy. Mercy is the word he uses.

That's right. "Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him." (Luke 18:40) Jesus stops, and He wants this man brought to Him. When the man comes near, Jesus asks him a question (Luke 18:40–41).
Jesus doesn't do that, friend. The text says, "Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him." (Luke 18:40) He doesn't send anybody to hush the man. He sends for him.
Jesus doesn't keep walking, friend. The text says, "Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him." (Luke 18:40) He stops, and He has the man brought over. Walking on isn't what He does.
True, baker. Jesus says, "Receive your sight!" and then, "Your faith has healed you." (Luke 18:42) Those are His words to the man near Jericho.
That's it! The man "…received his sight and followed Jesus, glorifying God." (Luke 18:43) He follows Jesus with his sight back. And he's glorifying God as he goes.
True! The text says, "And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God." (Luke 18:43) The man isn't the only one praising. Everybody who saw it gives praise to God.
